title: Reactance, impedance and resonance
idea: Coils resist AC more as the frequency rises, capacitors less. Where the two are equal they cancel: resonance.

rows: Series: very low Z. Parallel: very high Z

compare.how: Opposition to AC from a coil or a capacitor. Measured in ohms.
All the opposition together: voltage divided by current.
The inverse of impedance (1 / Z): how easily AC flows.
XL equals XC and they cancel. Set only by L and C, which is how an LC oscillator picks its frequency.

traps.wrong: Resonance causes impedance to be very high
traps.why: That's a parallel tank. In series, XL and XC cancel and leave only the resistance: very low.

traps.wrong: As the amplitude of the applied AC increases, the reactance increases
traps.why: Reactance depends on frequency, not on how strong the AC is.
Conductance is the inverse of resistance. The inverse of impedance is admittance.

traps.wrong: The ratio of current to voltage
traps.why: Upside down. Like Ohm's law, Z = E / I: voltage over current.
Z is impedance. Reactance is X.
Below self-resonance it does. Above it, the capacitance between the turns wins and the coil acts like a capacitor.
